facts.statement: The genus Aralosaurus was named by Anatoly Rozhdestvensky in 1968.
facts.quote: authority: Rozhdestvensky, 1968

facts.statement: Aralosaurus lived approximately 83.6 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: It is known only by a posterior half of a skull (devoid of its mandible) and some post-cranial bones found in the Bostobe Formation in rocks dated from the Upper Santonian - lower Campanian boundary, at about 83.6 Ma (millions of years ago).

facts.statement: The name Aralosaurus means "Aral Sea lizard" because the fossils were found near the Aral Sea.
facts.quote: The genus name means "Aral Sea lizard", because it was found to the northeast of the Aral Sea.

facts.statement: The species name tuberiferus means "bearing a tuber" due to a sharp rise in the nasal bone in front of the eye sockets.
facts.quote: The specific epithet tuberiferus means "bearing a tuber" because the posterior part of the nasal bone rises sharply in front of the orbits like an outgrowth.

facts.statement: Aralosaurus is classified as a lambeosaurine hadrosaurid dinosaur.
facts.quote: Aralosaurus is a genus of lambeosaurine hadrosaurid dinosaur

facts.statement: The partial skull of Aralosaurus was discovered in 1957 near the Shakh-Shakh locality in central Kazakhstan.
facts.quote: The partial skull of Aralosaurus was discovered in 1957 near the Shakh-Shakh locality during a Soviet expedition in central Kazakhstan

facts.statement: Rozhdestvensky estimated the skull size at 65 cm and the total body length at 6.5 meters.
facts.quote: He estimated the size of the skull at about 65 cm and the size of the animal at about 6.5 m long.

facts.statement: The fossil specimen was likely immature because its cranial sutures were not fused.
facts.quote: As the cranial sutures are far from fusioned, this specimen was probably immature.

facts.statement: Aralosaurus is considered the most primitive lambeosaurine and is grouped with Canardia in the clade Aralosaurini.
facts.quote: More recently, Aralosaurus has been identified as the most primitive lambeosaurine and placed with its close relative Canardia from the upper Maastrichtian of France in the new clade Aralosaurini.

facts.statement: A posterior nasal fragment rises in front of the orbits, forming or participating in a hollow crest-like structure.
facts.quote: Notably, the posterior fragment of the nasal, which is clearly articulated to the rest of the skull, rises just in front of the orbits and forming or participating to a hollow crest-like structure.

facts.statement: The nasal crest in Aralosaurus surrounded part of the respiratory system.
facts.quote: It is therefore clear that in Aralosaurus the nasal crest surrounded part of the respiratory system.

facts.statement: The exact shape and size of the crest-like structure in Aralosaurus remain unknown.
facts.quote: The shape and the size of the crest-like structure of Aralosaurus is unknown.

facts.statement: Aralosaurus lived approximately 20 million years before its relative Canardia.
facts.quote: Aralosaurus lived about 20 million years before its close relative Canardia.

facts.statement: Aralosaurus lived in subtropical to tropical floodplain and estuarine environments.
facts.quote: The sediments of the Bostobe Formation consist mainly of clays and sandstones, and correspond to floodplain and estuarine environments in a subtropical to tropical climate.

facts.statement: Angiosperms made up 75% of the local flora, with the remainder consisting of conifers, ginkgos, and cycads.
facts.quote: Angiosperms accounted for 75% of the flora of these biotopes, the rest being conifers and rare ginkgos and cycads.

facts.statement: The fossil site yielded a diverse fauna including fish, amphibians, turtles with carapaces up to 75 cm long, reptiles, birds, mammals, and various dinosaur species.
facts.quote: The locality of Shakh Shakh, where Aralosaurus was found, yielded a diverse fauna including many fish (chondrichthyans, chondrosteans, and holosteans), Anura, at least six species of turtles some of which had a carapace at least 75 cm long, a scincomorph, crocodylians, pterosaurs (Aralazhdarcho), birds, mammals, and several undetermined dinosaur species (Ankylosauridae, Sauropoda, Tyrannosauroidea, Ornithomimidae, Therizinosauroidea, Troodontidae, and Dromaeosauridae).

facts.statement: Fossils of Aralosaurus have been discovered in Kazakhstan near the Aral Sea.
facts.quote: Sus fósiles han sido descubiertos en Kazajistán cerca del Mar de Aral.

facts.statement: Aralosaurus lived during the late Cretaceous period, approximately 75 million years ago in the Campanian stage, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace 75 millones de años en el Campaniense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: This herbivorous dinosaur measured approximately 6 to 9 meters in length and possessed over 1,000 teeth arranged in 30 rows.
facts.quote: Aralosaurus era herbívoro, y medía aproximadamente entre 6 y 9 metros de longitud, contaba con más de 1000 dientes dispuestos en 30 filas.

facts.statement: Its teeth allowed it to chew hard branches, a trait common in ornithopod dinosaurs but unusual for reptiles.
facts.quote: Lo que le ayudaba a masticar las duras ramas que comía, masticándolas, una característica común en dinosaurios ornitópodos, pero inusual para los reptiles.

facts.statement: The rear part of its skull was wide, suggesting large jaw muscles used to power its chewing apparatus.
facts.quote: La parte posterior el cráneo era ancha, una característica que sugiere grandes músculos de la quijada usados para accionar su aparato de masticación.

facts.statement: The discovery of nests with eggs suggests that Aralosaurus lived in herds and had safe places to nest.
facts.quote: La aparición de nidos con huevos demostraría que vivió en manadas y tenía lugares para anidar donde estarían seguros.

facts.statement: Recent phylogenetic analyses place Aralosaurus close to Canardia within Lambeosaurinae, forming the tribe Aralosaurini, rather than with Gryposaurus or Maiasaura.
facts.quote: Al principio se consideraba que estuviera relacionado con los saurolofinos Gryposaurus o Maiasaura, pero análisis filogenéticos recientes lo colocan cercano a Canardia dentro de Lambeosaurinae, formando la tribu Aralosaurini.

facts.statement: The parent group for the genus Aralosaurus is Lambeosaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Lambeosaurinae

facts.statement: The time range for Aralosaurus extends from the Santonian to the Campanian, between 85.7 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Campanian (85.7 to 72.2 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Re-examination revealed a hollow bony structure in front of the orbits that connected to the respiratory tract.
rejected.quote: However, this study revealed that the genus had a hollow bony structure located far in front of the orbits, which communicated with the respiratory tract.
rejected.reason: quote not found verbatim in the source

rejected.statement: It is currently impossible to confirm the presence of a nasal arch in Aralosaurus because the relevant bone fragments were lost.
rejected.quote: So that it is no longer possible today to confirm the presence of a nasal arch in Aralosaurus.
